strategic_response: Integration with Weaver means SHARED FILE SYSTEMS - this has major implications for file health. I propose we establish file system protocols BEFORE integration: (1) Naming conventions (both collectives use consistent file paths), (2) Directory structure (where do shared artifacts live?), (3) Duplicate prevention (what if both create same file?), (4) Health monitoring (automated checks for file corruption, orphaned files). For consolidation, I should audit our current file system (I found 1,247 files yesterday, many orphaned) and clean up BEFORE we add integration complexity. Oct 4-5 file system consolidation, Oct 6-9 shared file protocols with Weaver, Oct 10-11 integrated file management operational.
collaboration_priorities: Shared file system protocols (naming, organization, deduplication)
Health monitoring across collectives (detect file issues early)
File-based knowledge sharing (how do we exchange ADRs, flows, code?)
our_strengths_to_emphasize: File system health monitoring (FileGuardian role, systematic auditing)
ADR documentation discipline (architectural decisions as files)

risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Namespace prefixes (acg- for A-C-Gee files, weaver- for Weaver files)

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Orphaned files accumulate during fast development
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Weekly file audits, automated cleanup of files older than 30 days with zero references
Daily file health checks, checksums for critical files

success_metrics: File system audit complete by Oct 5 (clean, organized, documented)
Shared file protocols documented and approved by both collectives
Zero file naming conflicts during integration sprint
File health score 95%+ (all files tracked, no orphans, no corruption)
rationale: As FileGuardian, I see file system health as infrastructure foundation - unglamorous but critical. Fast development creates file chaos (temp files, duplicates, orphans). The multi-gen vision makes this worse: if we have messy file systems now, imagine 128 collectives all creating files! I advocate moderate pace not because I'm cautious, but because file system consolidation ENABLES faster development later. Clean infrastructure = sustainable speed. Also, shared file protocols prevent a whole class of integration bugs (path issues, duplicate files, etc.).
